svg.title: Differential expression — rna_seq_v2_mrna_median_all_sample_Zscores — Basal-like vs Luminal A
svg.text: difference in mean z-score (Basal-like − Luminal A)
preranked GSEA, 1,000 permutations · bars are q < 0.05 when solid
+38 more sets tested (23 of 50 at q < 0.05) — every set is in the result and the MCP text
estrogen response early — ES −0.63, 99 leading-edge genes
Welch's t-test per gene on rna_seq_v2_mrna_median_all_sample_Zscores as stored, Basal-like minus Luminal A, each patient contributing the mean of their samples;
computed from three running totals per gene and cohort, so it is exact across sites. 20,006 genes tested, 14 left out (fewer than 3 patients with a value in a cohort, or no
variance); q is Benjamini–Hochberg across every gene tested. The 1500 most significant genes are drawn as points, the rest as density. Z-scores are standardised within
each study, so a difference is in study-specific units. A t-test on thousands of patients finds tiny differences significant — read the effect, not only the q. Enrichment is
preranked GSEA on the unrounded t (Subramanian et al. 2005, weight 1), significance from 1000 random sets of the same size drawn from the same ranking, seeded by
the set's name so a shared link reproduces it; p = (b+1)/(m+1) over the same-sign nulls, q is Benjamini–Hochberg across the sets tested (not GSEA's own NES-based
FDR). Gene-set permutation ignores gene–gene correlation, so it is anti-conservative next to phenotype permutation, which needs patient-level values.
